name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,663

clue.text: One tight-lipped with stuff changing hands

indicators.note: hands come as right and left, so one side's abbreviation is exchanged for the other's

blocks.note: to stuff is to cram, packing something tightly
the right hand (R) becomes the left (L)

explanation.surface: Someone keeps their mouth shut while goods are passed from one person to another.
explanation.walkthrough: CRAM with its R (right) swapped for L (left) gives CLAM; 'changing hands' sounds like a sale but means switching right for left.
explanation.definitionFit: A clam shuts its shell tight, and a person who will not talk is said to clam up, so the shellfish stands for a silent type.

clue.text: Leading actor Heather's role in film about Hannibal

blocks.note: the lead in a film
another name for common heather

explanation.surface: An actress called Heather has landed a part in a Hannibal film.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like an actress's first name, but it is the plant, ling. Clarice STARLING is the FBI trainee in The Silence of the Lambs.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarice Starling is the agent played by Jodie Foster opposite Anthony Hopkins's Hannibal Lecter in The Silence of the Lambs.

clue.text: Throw up over reserved person way over to the left

definitions.text: person way over to the left

indicators.note: turning something over flips it, so the letters run the other way in this down clue

blocks.note: to lob is to throw something high
a reserved person is shy

explanation.surface: Someone vomits on a quiet person whose politics are far left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw up' suggests being sick, but it is a lofted throw. BOLSHY (or bolshie) is British slang from Bolshevik, for a left-wing radical or an awkward, rebellious person.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for Bolshevik, the word names a radical socialist, someone whose politics sit at the far left of the spectrum.

clue.text: Tree planting succeeded south of cold Belgian city

indicators.note: in a down answer, being south of something means coming below it, so this piece follows the rest

blocks.note: C for cold, as on a tap
Ypres is a city in Flanders, Belgium
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: A tree-planting scheme has gone well in the south of a chilly Belgian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tree planting succeeded' reads as one phrase about a project, but only 'Tree' is the definition; S then goes beneath C and YPRES.
explanation.definitionFit: The cypress is a tall evergreen conifer, often planted in cemeteries and along Mediterranean roads.

clue.text: Money and time in treatment provide medical solution

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: tin is old slang for money
T is the abbreviation for time
a cure is a course of treatment

explanation.surface: With enough cash and time in therapy, you will find a medical answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solution' tempts toward the answer to a problem, but here it is a liquid medicine. Tin is old British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A tincture is a medicine dissolved in alcohol, so it is literally a solution used for treatment.

clue.text: Something fragrant from vase father repaired

indicators.note: something repaired has been taken apart and put back together, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Dad has mended a vase and something sweet-smelling comes out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The ten letters of the two words rearrange fully; the surface hints at flowers, but the scent is a man's grooming product.
explanation.definitionFit: Aftershave is a scented lotion men splash on after shaving, so it is something with a pleasant smell.

clue.text: Box to go in entrance essentially for snobs

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only the central letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: a portal is a grand entrance or doorway
the central letter of the three-letter word
the central letter of the five-letter word

explanation.surface: A box seat at the theatre, reached through a doorway reserved for the snobbish.
explanation.walkthrough: A Portaloo is a British brand of portable toilet cabin, as at festivals; 'go' means relieve oneself, and 'Box' suggests a theatre box.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable toilet is a plastic cubicle you go in to use the lavatory, informally a box for the purpose.

clue.text: Bit of a cheek having rear pinched by Hancock in sin

indicators.note: pinching means stealing, so losing the rear means the final letter is removed

blocks.note: a glute is a buttock muscle, part of a cheek of the bottom
Tony Hancock was a British radio and TV comedian of the 1950s and 60s

explanation.surface: Hancock gets a cheeky pinch on the bottom, which counts as a sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheek' sounds like impudence but means a buttock here, and 'pinched' plays on both a grope and a theft.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluttony, overindulgence in food and drink, is one of the seven deadly sins in Christian teaching.

clue.text: Flood possibly at home before hunter returned

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
the wolf is a pack hunter

explanation.surface: A flood may have struck the house before the huntsman got back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' marks the definition as an example: a flood is one kind of inflow, not the only one.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflow is any stream of water or other matter coming in, and a flood is a dramatic instance of that.

clue.text: Shades naked mums with undergarments

indicators.note: a naked thing has its covering stripped off, so the outer letters go and only the inside stays

blocks.note: the inner pair of letters once the outside ones are stripped
bras are women's undergarments

explanation.surface: Pictures of mothers in only their underwear, half-hidden in shadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naked' hints that the bras come off, but it is the mums that are stripped, of their first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbra is the darkest part of a shadow, so the plural is a set of shadows, which are also called shades.

clue.text: Only just exclude place with a cathedral

blocks.note: to exclude them
A small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England

explanation.surface: Someone is narrowly kept out of a cathedral town.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a favourite setter's city because its cathedral is famous and its name is so short.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases describe something that happens by the narrowest possible margin, scarcely managed.

clue.text: Starters of this easily paired with fresh claret

definitions.text: Starters of this easily paired with fresh claret

indicators.note: starters come at the start of a meal, so the opening letter of each word is taken
something made fresh is newly prepared, so the letters are remade in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A dish whose first bites go down easily with a glass of red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: 'this' points at the answer itself, which pairs well with wine. The rearranged red wine comes first, then the two initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Raclette is a Swiss dish of melted cheese scraped over potatoes, traditionally served with wine, so the description fits the meal.

clue.text: Colour of an articulated Laurie?

indicators.note: to articulate is to pronounce clearly, so the word is said out loud and spelt differently

blocks.note: Hugh Laurie is the English actor of House and Blackadder; the question mark marks a first name taken from a surname

explanation.surface: Asking what shade a jointed figure called Laurie is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articulated' suggests a jointed lorry or doll, but it means spoken. Laurie leads to the actor's first name, Hugh.
explanation.definitionFit: Hue is the standard word for a colour or a particular shade or tint.

clue.text: What chefs might use to dispel small talk

indicators.note: dispelling means driving something away, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: a herb used in cooking and as a garnish
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A cooking tool for getting rid of chit-chat in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small talk' reads as one phrase, but it splits: S is removed from the herb and 'talk' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A parley is a discussion or negotiation, especially between enemies, so it is a formal kind of talk.

clue.text: Stone that's the same as mine

blocks.note: first meaning: the hard seed of a fruit such as a cherry
second meaning: a coal mine or quarry

explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like a possessive, as in 'the same as my stone', but it is the noun for a colliery.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the hard kernel in a fruit and a hole dug to extract coal or minerals.

clue.text: One historically seen on Mount 11 26 perhaps

definitions.text: One historically seen on Mount 11 26 perhaps

blocks.note: surface reading: a figure from history spotted on a mountain called Mount Something
setter's reading: a noblewoman who, legend says, rode a horse through Coventry with no clothes on, the answer to 11 and 26

explanation.walkthrough: The capital M dresses 'Mount' as a mountain's name, but it is a horse. 11/26 is BARELY: she rode naked through Coventry, England, in protest at her husband's taxes.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleventh-century countess is famous solely for riding a horse through Coventry with nothing on but her long hair.

clue.text: Fabric of stars (type worn by Prince)

indicators.note: clothes worn by someone wrap around them, so these letters go around another

blocks.note: suns are stars
ilk means type or kind, as in 'of that ilk'
P is the abbreviation for prince

explanation.surface: The pop star Prince famously wore clothes made from a starry material.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket paints Prince's flamboyant stage wear, but 'Prince' is only the letter P, tucked in after the first letter of the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Spun silk is a cloth made from short waste silk fibres spun into yarn, so it is a type of textile.

clue.text: Cycles from back of vast mountain in range

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only its last letter is kept
being in something means lying inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
the Andes is the mountain range of South America
M is the map abbreviation for mountain

explanation.surface: Bike rides that start from the far side of a huge peak in a mountain chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycles' could mean recurring periods, but these are bicycles. M slips inside ANDES just before its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: A tandem is a bicycle built for two riders, one behind the other, so tandems are a kind of cycle.

clue.text: Rough Latino area on a peninsula

indicators.note: something rough is crude and unpolished, so the letters come out in a disordered state

blocks.note: taken as written
A is the abbreviation for area
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tough Latin American neighbourhood located on a spit of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough Latino area' paints a neighbourhood, but 'Rough' rearranges the six letters plus two As.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatolia, or Asia Minor, is the large peninsula forming the Asian part of modern Turkey.

clue.text: State measure of land needed for butchery

blocks.note: Mass. is the abbreviation for Massachusetts, a US state
an acre is a unit of land area

explanation.surface: A government declaring how much land a slaughterhouse requires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb meaning declare, but it is a US state in abbreviated form.
explanation.definitionFit: A massacre is the brutal killing of many people, which can also be called butchery or slaughter.

clue.text: Country requires French denial after Elba bombed

indicators.note: something bombed is blown apart, so its letters are scattered and rearranged
after sets the order, so the piece named before this word is placed second

blocks.note: taken as written
non is French for no

explanation.surface: A nation needs France to deny a bombing raid on the island of Elba.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the French word behind the rearranged island name.
explanation.definitionFit: Lebanon is a small nation on the eastern Mediterranean coast, between Syria and Israel.

clue.text: Drop wader that's been unwrapped

indicators.note: unwrapping takes off the outer layer, so the first and last letters are removed and the inside kept

blocks.note: the snipe is a long-billed wading bird; only its inner letters are kept

explanation.surface: Putting down a wading bird that has just been taken out of its packaging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop' looks like a verb, but it is a small measure of drink. 'wader' might suggest a boot, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A nip is a small measure of spirits, just as a drop is a small amount of a drink.

clue.text: Most of school team mates won't ultimately rub along

indicators.note: most but not all, so the last letter is dropped
ultimately means in the end, so the final letter of each word is taken

blocks.note: a coed is a co-educational school, for boys and girls together
XI is eleven in Roman numerals, the size of a cricket or football team
the last letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Most of the school team just won't get on with their teammates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mates won't ... rub along' reads as a quarrel, but the end letters of those two words are what count, and 'rub along' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To rub along is a British idiom for living or working together tolerably well, which is what coexisting means.

clue.text: Slimy vegetation across a grassland partly retreating

indicators.note: only part of the words is used, so the letters lie inside the run of text
retreating means moving backwards, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: letters running through the end of the first word, the whole of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Slimy plant life spreading across a meadow and partly pulling back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' looks like the container phrase but is part of the hidden run; read it backwards from 'grassland'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sargasso is a floating brown seaweed, giving its name to the Sargasso Sea, so it is slippery marine plant life.

clue.text: Get stronger buzzer to have fellow out of bed

blocks.note: a bee buzzes
F is the abbreviation for fellow
to be up is to be out of bed

explanation.surface: A louder alarm clock is needed to get a man out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buzzer' sounds like an alarm, but it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: To beef something up is an informal idiom for making it more powerful or substantial, that is, to strengthen it.

clue.text: Operation reversed drain in Times Square

indicators.note: something reversed is turned back to front, so its letters run the other way
being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within others

blocks.note: to sap is to drain someone's strength
by means times in multiplication, as in four by three
S is short for square, as in street-name abbreviations

explanation.surface: Work on a blocked drain in New York's Times Square has gone backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Times Square is New York's famous junction, but the two words split: BY for times, S for square, with the reversed drain between.
explanation.definitionFit: A bypass is a surgical procedure that reroutes blood around a blocked artery, a common heart operation.

clue.text: Destiny to become short and podgy

indicators.note: something short falls short of full length, so the last letter is cut

blocks.note: fate is destiny

explanation.surface: Someone fated to end up small and plump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short and podgy' reads as one description of a person, but 'short' is the cut and only 'podgy' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Podgy is a British informal word for slightly overweight or chubby, which is what being fat means.

clue.text: See 11
Commune of lovers accommodating comrade regularly

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so one piece is housed inside another
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: beaux are boyfriends or admirers
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A commune of free lovers takes in a fellow comrade now and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commune' sounds like a hippy collective, which the lovers and comrade build on, but it is a French local authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Bordeaux is a city in south-west France, and a commune is the basic French unit of local government.

clue.text: Awfully steep having to swallow fifty pounder

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so the letters come out in a messed-up order
swallowing takes something inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: taken as written
L is fifty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A terribly expensive bill means forking out fifty quid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pounder' looks like money (as in fifty pounds), but it is a tool that pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A pestle is the club-shaped tool used to crush and grind ingredients in a mortar, so it is something that pounds.

clue.text: Green accompaniment to 7 without the alcohol

definitions.text: Green accompaniment to 7 without the alcohol

blocks.note: surface reading: something green served alongside a portable toilet, absurdly
setter's reading: take PORT from the answer to 7 to leave ALOO, potato, and this leafy spinach is its partner in a curry-house dish

explanation.walkthrough: The answer at 7 is PORTALOO; remove the fortified wine and ALOO remains. Saag aloo is a popular Indian side of spinach and potato.
explanation.definitionFit: In Indian cooking the word means leafy greens, usually spinach, as in the classic pairing with potato.

clue.text: See 2
Metal slice setter moved back

indicators.note: moving something back shifts it to an earlier spot, so the letter is reinserted nearer the start

blocks.note: a sliver is a thin slice
the setter refers to themselves as I

explanation.surface: A metal blade that the person who sets it has pushed back into place.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's I is lifted out of the thin slice and put back one place earlier, ahead of the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver is a precious metallic element, chemical symbol Ag, used in jewellery and coins.

clue.text: Bears in America from the East with spots?

indicators.note: coming from the east means travelling west, right to left on a map, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: US is short for the United States of America
stains are spots or marks

explanation.surface: Are there spotted bears in the eastern parts of the United States?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bears' looks like the animals, which suits 'in America', but it is the verb meaning supports.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain a load is to carry or hold up its weight, just as a beam bears or supports it.
